title: Prope migration manifest
description: What a scan of an application found. A proposal a person reviews before anything is uploaded or rewritten. ADR-0066.

version.description: Manifest format version. register.py refuses anything else rather than guessing.

scanned_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the scan. Informational.

repository.description: How the scanned repository identifies itself. Informational; never sent to Prope.

notes.description: Anything the reviewer should know before reading the rows: a directory that was skipped, a wrapper that could not be traced, a framework whose prompts live outside the repository.

namespace.description: PROPOSED folder. Also the access container, and immutable once created (A-021, ADR-0061) - a prompt cannot be moved out of it, ever. Derive it from where the prompt lives in THIS repository, in this team's vocabulary.

name.description: PROPOSED name within the folder. Immutable once created; it is what the consuming code will call.

title.description: Human-readable, for the prompt list. Not an identifier.

purpose.description: What this prompt is for, in a sentence. Feeds the search corpus; worth writing.

body.description: The prompt as canonical XML: a flat sequence of system/context/instructions/output_format/examples/constraints blocks, no nesting, no attributes, no text outside a block. Placeholders are {{name}}. This must be what the application runs TODAY - reorganised into blocks, never rewritten.

variables.description: Every {{name}} in the body, with where its value comes from.

source_expression.description: The expression interpolated at the call site, verbatim - `today`, `user.tier`. This is what phase 4 passes as variables={...}.

inferred.description: True when the source carried no name (positional %s, a tuple index) and the scanner chose one. A reviewer should look at every inferred variable.

sources.description: Where this prompt lives and where it is called. The reviewer's way back to the code.

kind.description: definition = where the text lives; call_site = where it reaches an LLM client; assembly = where several fragments are concatenated into the final body.

enclosing.description: The function or class containing it. Context for the reviewer, NOT a relationship claim - static chain recovery is deliberately out of scope (OQ-155).

runtime.description: The language or runtime this source is written in - python, typescript, javascript, go, ruby, java, browser. REQUIRED on a call_site, because the SDK is Python and a call site in anything else cannot be rewritten to use it. A reviewer who learns that after registering forty immutable prompt names has learned it too late.

upstream_model.description: The provider model this call currently uses, as found in the source. Recorded so whoever approves the revision can bind the same one; the scanner never chooses it.

parameters.description: Provider parameters found at the call site - temperature, max_tokens. Carried across so the migration does not silently change behaviour.

name_confidence.description: How sure the scanner is about namespace/name. Anything below high is a row the reviewer must stop on, because the choice is permanent.

warnings.description: Anything that made extraction uncertain: a body assembled across files, a conditional fragment, a template loaded by a path computed at runtime. Say it here rather than guessing quietly.

original_body.description: The prompt EXACTLY as it appears in the source, before you reorganised it into canonical blocks - whitespace, wording and all. Prope stores it beside the canonical body so a reviewer can answer 'is this the same prompt?' from the row instead of from a text editor, and so the conversion stays auditable after the source file changes. Omit only when the source was already canonical XML.

original_format.description: What original_body is written in. 'xml' means the source was already canonical and nothing was converted. Anything else records a conversion and requires original_body.

original_filename.description: Basename of the file the body came from - `planner.xml`, `prompts.py`. No directories.
